- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.0) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative (sentiment < -0.3) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Lag in price correction: model often lags 1–3 days behind true price movements, especially after sharp sentiment shifts.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility and fails to smoothly revert to historical mean in 30-day horizon.
- Overshoot after positive sentiment spikes — model forecasts peak too high, then drops sharply, missing the true peak’s timing.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model tends to overforecast — especially in early days of the 30-day window.
- Avoid extrapolating sentiment trends too far — sentiment decay or reversal often undercuts model’s momentum.
